claims.claim: US minimum-parking mandates were first widely enacted in the 1950s to keep street parking from becoming overcrowded.
claims.episode_span: Cities adopted minimum-parking rules in the mid-twentieth century as a way to prevent on-street congestion, copying standards that treated parking as an automatic companion to any new building.
claims.supporting_quote: Parking minimums were first enacted in 1950s America during the post-war construction boom with the intention of preventing street parking from becoming overcrowded.

claims.claim: Donald Shoup's 2005 book The High Cost of Free Parking documents the negative repercussions of off-street parking requirements.
claims.episode_span: Donald Shoup’s research has documented how these mandates spread from a few model ordinances into thousands of municipal codes
claims.supporting_quote: His 2005 book The High Cost of Free Parking identifies the negative repercussions of off-street parking requirements

claims.claim: Shoup advocated pricing curb parking and dedicating the meter revenue to public services, and many US cities have followed his research.
claims.episode_span: Pricing curb space at rates that clear demand, as Shoup has long advocated, would reduce the pressure to overbuild off-street inventory
claims.supporting_quote: His research on municipal parking policies has led numerous cities throughout the United States to change the price of curb parking and to dedicate the resulting parking meter revenue to finance added public services in the metered districts.

claims.claim: Structured parking costs on the order of tens of thousands of dollars per space: roughly $28,000 average for an above-ground structure and about $56,000 for an underground spot, excluding land.
claims.episode_span: structured parking costs tens of thousands of dollars per space
claims.supporting_quote: A parking structure costs an average of $28,000 per spot, and an underground one about $56,000 per spot, excluding the cost of land.

claims.claim: Parking minimums shift parking costs onto developers as a hidden cost that is passed through in rents, so even car-free households pay for parking.
claims.episode_span: Even households that never own a vehicle end up subsidizing those spaces through higher rents or markups, because the cost is baked into the project before any tenant arrives.
claims.supporting_quote: Parking minimums have shifted the cost of parking spaces from drivers to building developers, making them a hidden cost
